info.text: Unit 22 — Calling OEM / vendor technical support. Listening, Reading, Use of English and Vocabulary.

name.text: U22-L1 where the display fault happens

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. When does the display fault always happen?

generalfeedback.text: Ravil says the fault appears always during taxi, and the team could not reproduce it while the aircraft was parked.

feedback.text: Correct — "always during taxi".
No — the fault is a ground event during taxi, not in the cruise.
No — they could not reproduce it while parked.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The BITE test passed and stored no fault. True or false?

generalfeedback.text: Ravil: "Yesterday we ran the BITE test, but it passed and stored no fault." So the statement is true.

feedback.text: Correct — it passed and stored nothing.
Listen again — the test passed and stored no fault.

name.text: U22-L3 how many times this week

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many times did the team see the fault this week? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: "The fault code is DU-204, and we saw it four times this week." Answer: 4.

feedback.text: Correct — four times this week.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. For about how many seconds does the display blank? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: "It blanks for about one second, then it comes back on its own." Answer: 1.

feedback.text: Correct — about one second.

name.text: U22-L5 how many weeks the radio fault lasted

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. For how many weeks had the radio fault been on the aircraft? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: "For three weeks. Although we changed the antenna cable, the fault did not go away." Answer: 3.

feedback.text: Correct — three weeks.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. On the bench, what did the removed radio do?

generalfeedback.text: "On the bench it passed every time. That is why we suspect a wiring or connector problem." The unit is fine; the fault is on the aircraft side.

feedback.text: Correct — it passed on the bench, so the fault is on the aircraft.

answer.text: It failed with a no-comm fault

feedback.text: No — it failed on the aircraft, but passed on the bench.

answer.text: It could not be tested at all

feedback.text: No — the bench test ran and the radio passed.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The team changed the antenna cable and the fault went away. True or false?

generalfeedback.text: "Although we changed the antenna cable, the fault did not go away." So the statement is false.

feedback.text: Correct — the fault did not go away.
Listen again — "although we changed the antenna cable, the fault did not go away".

questiontext.text:
Read this BITE readout.

BITE READOUT — VHF-2
Test result : FAIL
Stored fault : no-comm, intermittent
Last seen    : during taxi
Recommended  : inspect the connector; do not swap the LRU
Reference    : service bulletin SB 23-070

What action does the readout recommend?

generalfeedback.text: The readout says "inspect the connector; do not swap the LRU". So the recommended action is to inspect the connector.

feedback.text: Correct — that is the recommended action.

answer.text: Swap the LRU for a new one

feedback.text: No — the readout says "do not swap the LRU".

answer.text: Escalate the fault to the desk

feedback.text: No — escalation is not mentioned in the readout.

name.text: U22-R2 readout says swap the LRU

questiontext.text: Read the BITE readout again (VHF-2, above). The readout tells you to swap the LRU. True or false?

generalfeedback.text: The readout says "do not swap the LRU". So the statement is false.

feedback.text: Correct — it says do NOT swap the LRU.
Read again — the readout says "do not swap the LRU".

name.text: U22-R3 how often the fault appears

questiontext.text: Read the BITE readout again (VHF-2, above). The stored fault is "intermittent". How often does the fault appear?

generalfeedback.text: "Intermittent" means it happens on and off — only sometimes, not all the time.

feedback.text: Correct — intermittent = on and off.
No — that would be a constant fault, not intermittent.
No — "intermittent" is the opposite of constant.

questiontext.text:
Read this work order.

WORK ORDER WO-90211 — Aircraft YL-BCS
Task     : repair the wiring behind the number one display
Steps    : the team found a chafed wire near the connector;
           they fitted a new backshell
Check    : after the repair, the BITE test was clear
Follow-up: functional check due on the next taxi
Note     : service bulletin SB 34-118

What did the team find?

generalfeedback.text: The Steps line says the team "found a chafed wire near the connector". That was the root cause.

feedback.text: Correct — a chafed wire near the connector.
No — the fault was in the wiring, not the screen.

answer.text: A leak in the fuel line

feedback.text: No — this is an avionics wiring job, not a fuel job.

questiontext.text: Read the work order again (WO-90211, above). After the repair, the BITE test was clear. True or false?

generalfeedback.text: The Check line says "after the repair, the BITE test was clear". So the statement is true.

feedback.text: Correct — the BITE test was clear after the repair.
Read again — the Check line says the test was clear.

questiontext.text:
Write the verb in the past simple. Write one word.

Yesterday we ______ (run) the BITE test.

generalfeedback.text: Irregular verb: run → ran. A past time word ("yesterday") needs the past form.

feedback.text: Correct — run → ran.

name.text: U22-U2 base verb after did not

questiontext.text:
Write the correct verb form. Write one word.

We did not ______ (find) a stored fault.

generalfeedback.text: After did / did not use the base verb: find. The word did already shows the past.

feedback.text: Correct — base verb after "did not".

questiontext.text:
Write the missing word to make a past-simple question. Write one word.

______ you inspect the connector?

generalfeedback.text: Past-simple questions begin with Did + subject + base verb: "Did you inspect the connector?"

feedback.text: Correct — "Did you inspect…?"
Correct — "Did you inspect…?"

questiontext.text:
Write the verb in the past simple. Write one word.

This morning the team ______ (fit) a spare LRU.

generalfeedback.text: fit → fitted (double the t, add -ed). The ending sounds like /ɪd/ — an extra syllable, "fit-id".

feedback.text: Correct — fit → fitted.

questiontext.text:
Write the missing article. Write one word.

We replaced ______ valve yesterday.

generalfeedback.text: English needs the before a known part. Latvian and Russian have no articles, so this word is easy to drop.

feedback.text: Correct — "the valve".

questiontext.text:
Write the bank term for the meaning. Write one word.

A temporary fix you use until the real parts arrive is a ______.

generalfeedback.text: workaround — a temporary way to keep working until the real fix is ready.

feedback.text: Correct — a workaround.
Correct — usually written "workaround".

questiontext.text:
Write the bank term for the meaning. Write two words.

The aircraft book where you record faults and work is the ______ .

generalfeedback.text: tech log — the aircraft technical log where faults and work are recorded.

feedback.text: Correct — the tech log.
Correct — the tech (technical) log.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: LRU = a box you can swap on the aircraft · connector = the plug that joins two parts · bench test = a test of a removed unit in the shop · service bulletin = an OEM document about a change or fix · root cause = the real first reason for the fault.

answer.text: a box you can swap on the aircraft
the plug that joins two parts
a test of a removed unit in the shop
an OEM document about a change or fix
the real first reason for the fault

questiontext.text: Match each verb to the noun it goes with.

generalfeedback.text: run a BITE test · raise a work order · clear the fault code · follow the recommendation · reproduce the fault. These verb + noun pairs make your English sound natural.

name.text: U22-V3 which term is the plug

questiontext.text: Which term means the plug that joins two parts of a wire or a unit?

generalfeedback.text: A connector is the plug that joins two parts. A wiring diagram is a drawing; a serial number names one single unit.

feedback.text: Correct — the connector is the plug.
No — that is the drawing of the connections.
No — that is the unique number for one unit.

name.text: U22-V4 which term is the advice

questiontext.text: Which term means the advice the specialist gives on what to do next?

generalfeedback.text: A recommendation is the advice on what to do next. Troubleshooting is the finding of the cause; a service bulletin is an OEM document.

feedback.text: Correct — the specialist's advice.
No — that is the work of finding the cause.
No — that is an OEM document about a change or fix.
